svg.title: Atomic structure overview
svg.desc: Particles & isotopes: Tiny positive nucleus: protons + neutrons; negative electrons in energy levels. Z = protons; A = protons + neutrons. Isotopes differ in neutrons. Losing electrons forms positive ions. Evidence changes models: Electron → plum pudding. Alpha scattering → tiny dense nucleus, mostly empty space. Bohr: specific levels; Chadwick: neutrons. Absorb radiation → electron rises; emit → falls. Decay & equations: Random nuclear decay. Activity in Bq = decays/s; detector count rate may be lower. Alpha: A−4, Z−2. Beta-minus: A unchanged, Z+1. Gamma: A and Z unchanged. Half-life: Time for activity/undecayed nuclei to halve. After n half-lives, (½)ⁿ remains. Subtract background first. After 3 half-lives, 1/8 remains and 7/8 has decayed. Hazards & uses: Contamination = radioactive material present; irradiation = exposure. Alpha especially harmful inside. Gamma tracers; targeted treatment. Match half-life and penetration to use; balance benefit and dose. Fission & fusion: Fission: large nucleus absorbs neutron → splits, releasing energy, neutrons and gamma. Neutrons can cause a chain reaction. Fusion: light nuclei join; some mass becomes radiation energy.
